ctx.en: As the children's fight got worse, a neighbour couldn't stand by and stepped in to stop it.

bad.s: ホラー映画[えいが]が怖[こわ]すぎて、{見[み]るに見[み]かねて}目[め]を閉[と]じた。
bad.en: (meant: the horror film was so scary I shut my eyes)
bad.why: It is about someone else's plight moving you to step in, not fright. Say kowakute mite irarenakatta.

bad.s: 久[ひさ]しぶりに会[あ]った孫[まご]がかわいくて、{見[み]るに見[み]かねて}抱[だ]きしめた。
bad.en: (meant: my grandchild was so cute I couldn't resist hugging them)
bad.why: It is only for a distressing situation you cannot leave alone, never for something delightful.

r: はれものにさわるよう
mean: treating someone as if walking on eggshells
lit: as if touching a swelling: handling someone as gingerly as a painful boil

use.how: 腫れ物に触るように + 扱う/接する, or 腫れ物に触るような態度: treating a touchy or hurt person with nervous over-caution so as not to set them off.

near.diff: 気を遣う is ordinary consideration for others; 腫れ物に触るよう is tense, nervous caution because the person might blow up or break down.

cue: Since the promotion fell through, nobody in the office dares mention it; everyone tiptoes around the colleague and weighs every word.

ctx.s: 試験[しけん]に落[お]ちた兄[あに]に、家族[かぞく]は{腫[は]れ物[もの]に触[さわ]るように}接[せっ]した。
ctx.en: The family tiptoed around my brother after he failed his exam.

ctx.s: 「そんな{腫[は]れ物[もの]に触[さわ]るような}態度[たいど]、やめてよ。普通[ふつう]にしてて。」
ctx.en: "Stop walking on eggshells around me. Just act normal."

ctx.s: 社長[しゃちょう]の機嫌[きげん]が悪[わる]い日[ひ]は、社員全員[しゃいんぜんいん]が{腫[は]れ物[もの]に触[さわ]るように}接[せっ]している。
ctx.en: On days when the president is in a bad mood, all the staff walk on eggshells around him.

ctx.s: 思春期[ししゅんき]の娘[むすめ]を{腫[は]れ物[もの]に触[さわ]るように}扱[あつか]うのは、かえってよくない。
ctx.en: Treating your teenage daughter as if she might break at any moment actually does more harm than good.

ctx.s: 彼[かれ]は怒[おこ]りっぽいので、周[まわ]りは{腫[は]れ物[もの]に触[さわ]るような}付[つ]き合[あ]い方[かた]をしている。
ctx.en: He's quick to anger, so the people around him handle him with kid gloves.

ctx.s: あの事故[じこ]以来[いらい]、職場[しょくば]ではその話題[わだい]を{腫[は]れ物[もの]に触[さわ]るように}扱[あつか]っている。
ctx.en: Since that accident, everyone at work treats the subject with nervous caution.

bad.s: 看護師[かんごし]さんが{腫[は]れ物[もの]に触[さわ]るように}優[やさ]しくしてくれて、とても嬉[うれ]しかった。
bad.en: (meant: the nurse was so warmly gentle with me, I was really grateful)
bad.why: It implies tense, nervous over-caution, not warm kindness. To thank someone say yasashiku teinei ni sesshite kureta.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は{腫[は]れ物[もの]に触[さわ]るよう}な人[ひと]だ。
bad.en: (meant: he is a touchy person)
bad.why: It describes how others treat a touchy person, not the person. Say kare wa okorippoi, or kare ni haremono ni sawaru you ni sessuru.
